title: What this mockup shows

rows: Ideas from the updated model, for review.
Each screen says whether Jake asked for it, ChatGPT proposed it, or it is still undecided.
Nothing here is a working beta.

caption: A low-fidelity mockup of the updated model. Each screen says where its idea came from. All fictional; nothing is built.

title: A finite deck of entries
basis: Jake asked: about nine entries, swipe or random · Deck controls: ChatGPT proposal

screen.head: Choose what draws you in · card 4 of 9
rows: Two routes, one map
A group can't agree on the way home. What pulls your attention first?
Unreviewed prototype example.
Swipe for the next card. After nine, the deck ends.

caption: Jake asked for about nine entries to swipe through or pick at random. This proposed deck is finite and shuffled per visit; the person chooses.

title: Browse all nine

screen.head: All nine entries (unreviewed prototype examples)
rows: Morning on the trail · Reading the swell · The unanswered message
Two routes, one map · Market-day noise · A borrowed tool
The late train · Kitchen-table budget · A shared field

caption: Browse all shows every option without swiping. All nine titles are invented placeholders.

title: Surprise me

screen.head: Surprise me
rows: Picked: Market-day noise
Chosen at random from the nine, not from anything about you.
Shuffling is a discovery aid, not an experiment.

caption: A random pick only helps people start. It never assigns an entry from who they seem to be.

title: Same practice behind every card

screen.head: Notice · exercise notice-v1
rows: Notice where your attention keeps returning.
Then let in other parts of experience: sounds, light, touch, whatever is there.
No particular sensation is needed.
Placeholder text, awaiting review.

caption: Every card leads to the same shared practice. Nine entries are not nine exercises.

title: Motivation, in their own terms

screen.head: Motivation
rows: What moves you here, in your words?
Your words: "Wanting to be heard over the noise."
Other answers: mixed · uncertain · this framing doesn't fit me · skip

caption: Motivation in their own words; they can reject the framing itself. Nothing is scored.

title: Discern, respond, finish
basis: Discern/respond: original specification · Endings: ChatGPT proposal

screen.head: Discern · Respond · Finish
rows: Know: the stall is loud. I guess (mine): they don't care. Unsure: if it bothers others.
Next: act · ask · pause · leave. Chosen: pause.
Finish: keep · explore further · pause here · finish for now. All equal.
Chosen: keep. Saved on this device only.

caption: Known, guessed and unsure stay separate. They choose to pause, then keep the reflection; no ending counts as best.

title: Optional value signals
basis: Jake asked: signs of value from behaviour, no formal study · Signal list: ChatGPT proposal

screen.head: Help the beta learn? (optional)
rows: If you agree, the beta counts only: whether you saved, which ending you chose, whether you came back, whether you added to a reflection.
Never your words. Off unless you turn it on.
These are hints, not proof that it helped.

caption: Jake wanted signs of value without a survey question. Counting saves and returns is one proposal: a hint, not proof.

title: Return and revise

screen.head: Saved 3 days ago · Market-day noise
rows: Original (unchanged): "Wanting to be heard over the noise."
Added today: "The stallholder was shouting to be heard too."
Still unsure: whether to say anything.

caption: Returning and adding to a reflection may signal value. The original stays as it was.

title: What changed, if anything?
basis: Jake asked: room beyond Global Attentiveness

screen.head: What changed for you? (any, or none)
rows: Noticed something new · Understood another view · Became more unsure · Found a choice · Nothing changed
Global Attentiveness is one guiding question among several.
More uncertainty can be a good result.

caption: Global Attentiveness stays a guiding question, but people can report other changes, or none.

title: Propose a strategy
basis: Jake asked: users and groups suggest strategies · Fields: ChatGPT proposal

screen.head: Your strategy (private)
rows: Name: "Say back what I heard first"
Why it might help (my guess): people ease off when they feel heard.
Steps: repeat their point; ask if I got it right. Risk: can feel fake.
If ever shared, credit as: named · pseudonym · anonymous (proposed).
Kept private. Submitting to the team: undecided.

caption: People propose their own strategy and can try it "as if". It stays private unless they choose otherwise.

title: Try it, then review

screen.head: Strategy trial · version 1
rows: Intended: a calmer exchange.
Observed: they kept talking; I felt less rushed.
Version 2: "Only when I'm unsure what they meant."
Popularity is never shown as proof that a strategy works.

caption: Intended and observed effects stay separate; the strategy can be revised. Popularity is not evidence.

title: Three parties, more than three views
basis: Jake asked: multi-party, multilingual readiness · Model: ChatGPT proposal

screen.head: Fictional example · A shared field
rows: Parties: orchard families · grazing co-op · town council
Grazing co-op, member 1: "Close the path in lambing season."
Grazing co-op, member 2: "Keep it open; we need visitors."
Orchard families and co-op: disagree on timing. Council and co-op: unknown.

caption: A fictional three-party example. One party holds two views; no group speaks with one voice.

title: Original words and translation
basis: Jake asked: different languages and cultures · Display: ChatGPT proposal

screen.head: Original and translation
rows: Original (Spanish, words of co-op member 2): "Este campo es nuestra querencia."
Candidates: "our home ground" · "where we belong" · "where we draw strength"
Contributor: none of these quite fits.
Unresolved. Not a reviewed translation.

caption: The original stays beside possible translations, and the gap in meaning is kept. Language says nothing about identity.

title: Invitation to a private group
basis: Jake asked tentatively · Controls: ChatGPT proposal

screen.head: Invitation · Practice circle (fictional)
rows: Purpose: try one strategy on a fictional scenario.
Before joining: purpose, members, what is visible.
Separate choices: join · see shared items · add a strategy · evaluation · research data.
Joining shares nothing private. The admin role gives no access to private journals.
Undecided: invite caps, expiry, who can create groups.

caption: A tentative group path. An invitation is not membership, membership is not access to private reflections, and each permission is a separate choice.

title: Share one chosen item

screen.head: Share with Practice circle?
rows: Selected: strategy "Say back what I heard first" (v2)
Not selected: your reflections and answers.
Preview first. Nothing is sent in this mockup.

caption: Sharing is item by item, with a preview. Only a strategy is shared here.

title: Open question 1: private or group?

screen.head: Not resolved
rows: Proposed: no account; private reflection stays on this device.
Groups would need some identity, membership, shared content and a way to revoke.
How both can hold is not decided.

caption: The beta proposes on-device reflection with no account, but groups need shared identity. This mockup picks no answer.

title: Open question 2: AI later

screen.head: Not resolved
rows: Proposed for the first beta: no AI.
An earlier mockup showed a scripted voice conversation with a simulated AI.
That shows one possible style. It is not evidence that AI belongs in the first beta.

caption: The first beta is proposed without AI. The earlier voice video is a separate idea, not a reason to add AI.

title: What still needs deciding

rows: Real entry content, languages and reviewers.

Outcome dimensions; whether strategies can be submitted.
